newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to lodge complaint against Egypt on tuna.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to lodge complaint against Egypt on tuna.

text.p: Thailand will lodge a complaint with the World Trade Organization against Egypt, claiming Cairo has set up trade barriers against Thai canned tuna, a senior commerce ministry official said.
The official, who asked not to be identified, said Cairo has unfairly treated the Thai products which are now occupying the biggest market share of canned tuna in Egypt.

He claimed that Egypt made stringent quality requirements on canned tuna from Thailand such as demanding that the water content in the fish must not exceed five percent and nitrogen not exceed 40 percent.
"Even developed countries do not make such demand on quality. The cost of production will surge if we are to meet the requirements...it is almost impossible to do so," he said.

Moreover, Thai exporters must receive a certificate of guarantee from the Egyptian embassy in Bangkok before shipping the product to the country. The official claimed that the process took time and carries high cost.
He said the commerce ministry will gather evidence and present it to WTO, but did not provide the time frame.
Thailand exported 6.5 billion baht ($250 million) worth of canned tuna to Egypt during the first half of 1996 and held 88.2 percent of the market share, according to the oficial.
